date: 261029
reviewer: opus-architect (improvements only; plan not executed)
verdict: formula shape OK, but plan misses existing code (handoff note path) and the fact that ctx >= T at every rotation, so most of the adaptive range is dead. 9 improvements.

## facts found (code, not in scout file)
- f1 internal/harness/repl.go:27 `opusSonnetThreshold = 270_000`; repl.go:689 `effectiveThreshold()` returns 270k for opus/sonnet, else `a.Threshold` (flag default 80_000, repl.go:860). T already exists in code.
- f2 repl.go:517-518 `ctx := ctxTokens(usage); r.lastCtx = ctx` -> ctx is tokens from the last result usage (= "result_ctx"). Same unit as T. repl.go:921 resets lastCtx to 0 on new session.
- f3 repl.go:757 rotation fires only when `r.lastCtx >= thr` (after an answer). So at handoff-write time ctx >= T always (can overshoot by one turn).
- f4 repl.go:29 `handoffPrompt` (code-generated handoff note, "Be exact and brief", no length number). handoff.go:47 `validateHandoff` already rejects notes < 200 runes (utf8.RuneCountInString), retried via attempts (repl.go:633). A code hook for an upper cap already has a natural place.
- f5 repl.go:559 snapshot = trunc(join(parts), a.SnapshotChars), default 24000 (repl.go:865). Handoff note is one part of that snapshot.
- f6 classifier.go:31 planHint tells Haiku to write notes/runs/<YYMMDD>-plan-<topic>.md; no length rule. This is the only path for the plan/overview file (hybrid rule 6).

## improvements
1. Define "overview" (DECISION for user). Two different artifacts exist: (A) handoff note written at rotation (f4, code), (B) Haiku plan/overview file per workstream (f6, hybrid rule 6). DECISIONS:41 sits under [rotate], which points to (A).
   plan edit: add to (a): "overview = (A) handoff note at rotation and/or (B) plan file in notes/runs/. 사용자 확인 필요 (DECISION). Default proposal: both, same formula." Replace open question 6 with this.

2. Dead adaptive range for (A) (fact f3). At rotation ctx >= T, so cap for (A) is always >= 1.5 x base: Haiku >= 4,500, Opus/Sonnet >= 9,000 (hits 10,000 at ctx ~= 315k). Scaling below T only matters for (B), written mid-session.
   plan edit: in (b) Shape replace the "above T ... only if rotation does not happen" line with: "(A) handoff: ctx >= T by construction (repl.go:757), so cap = 1.5 x base up to CEIL. (B) plan file: ctx in [0, T), full range applies." Add acceptance row: Haiku, ctx 80,000 -> 4,500.

3. Haiku never reaches the user's 10,000 max (DECISION). With base 3,000, cap = 10,000 needs ctx = 2.83 x T = 226k, which the 80k rotation prevents; effective Haiku max ~= 4,500-4,800. If the user meant "both models may reach 10,000", the formula must change, e.g. cap = base + (CEIL - base) x min(ctx/T, 1) (Haiku 3,000->10,000, Opus 6,000->10,000 over [0, T]).
   plan edit: add open question: "Haiku 최대치가 약 4,500자에 머무는 것이 의도인지, 아니면 두 모델 모두 T에서 10,000자에 도달해야 하는지. 사용자 확인 필요 (DECISION)." Keep the current formula as option 1, the linear-to-CEIL one as option 2, with a 3-row table each.

4. Direction (DECISION, recommend grow). Purpose of the overview is to replace history the reader will not see; more context -> more to carry -> longer note. Shrinking saves tokens only on the reader side, and the reader (new session) starts near ctx 0, so the saving is small (<= 10,000 chars ~= 3-5k tokens once). Shrinking also contradicts the user's "최대 10,000자" (a max only makes sense if it grows).

Do not use the new session's ctx (~0 after reset, repl.go:921). Unit question is moot: ctx/T is a ratio, both in tokens.

# Plan: adaptive overview length cap

date: 261029
status: plan only, document only, no code or rule edits
user (Korean, verbatim): "개요 길이 상한(현재 Haiku 3,000자, Opus·Sonnet 6,000자 고정)을 상황에 따라 유기적으로 조정되게 변경, 최대 10000자."
inputs: notes/DECISIONS.md (last rows), CLAUDE.md (line 27 thresholds), notes/runs/261029-plan-hybrid-design.md (rule 6, open item 3)
facts file: notes/FACTS.md has no entries, nothing cited from it

## (a) Current fixed caps and where they are recorded
- Haiku overview: 3,000 chars. Opus and Sonnet overview: 6,000 chars. Both fixed.
- recorded in: notes/DECISIONS.md:41 (last row, 2026-10-29 user decision, "no existing code limit").
- CLAUDE.md: no cap stated (checked by grep for 3000/6000/overview). Not recorded there.
- notes/runs/261029-plan-hybrid-design.md: cap marked "사용자 확인 필요" at rule 6 (line 47) and open item 3 (line 93). The hybrid plan does not carry the 3,000/6,000 values.
- Related thresholds used for scaling (CLAUDE.md:27, DECISIONS:41): rotation threshold T = Haiku main 80k; Opus and Sonnet main 270k. Auto-compaction window 150k (CLAUDE.md:27).

## (b) Proposed adaptive rule
Inputs per overview write:
- base = 3,000 (Haiku main) or 6,000 (Opus or Sonnet main).
- ctx = current session context size, same unit as T (see open question 1).
- T = rotation threshold of the current main model (Haiku 80,000; Opus and Sonnet 270,000).

Formula:
- cap = clamp( base × (0.5 + ctx / T), FLOOR, CEIL )
- CEIL = 10,000 chars (user maximum).
- FLOOR = 1,000 chars (chosen here, not from the user; guards against very small or negative values; see open question 3).
- cap is rounded to the nearest 100 chars.
- ctx unknown: use cap = base (no scaling). Stated here as a fallback, not a user decision.

Shape:
- at ctx = 0, cap = 0.5 × base.
- at ctx = T, cap = 1.5 × base.
- above T: the main session is rotated at T, so this range only applies if rotation does not happen; cap keeps growing until CEIL.
- Direction (cap grows with context) is a proposal; see open question 2.

## (c) Where the rule is applied
- placeholder: to be located. Pointer: notes/runs/261029-scout-overview-cap.md (exists; scout found no code or CLAUDE.md rule for the cap, only DECISIONS.md:41). Its finding: no Go code writes the overview; Haiku writes it via planHint (classifier.go:31), so a code-level cap needs a hook in that writer, which does not exist yet. Exact file and line for the rule are not decided here.
- candidate place once located: hybrid plan rule 6 (notes/runs/261029-plan-hybrid-design.md:47) replaces "Length cap = 사용자 확인 필요" with the formula in (b).
- not applied to: chat replies (no fixed cap today; CLAUDE.md:21 says length follows content), agent result summaries (DECISIONS:36).

## (d) Acceptance: formula with 3 example inputs
Formula: cap = clamp( base × (0.5 + ctx / T), 1,000, 10,000 ), rounded to 100.

| # | model | base | ctx | T | 0.5 + ctx/T | raw | cap (chars) |
|---|-------|------|-----|---|-------------|-----|-------------|
| 1 | Haiku | 3,000 | 20,000 | 80,000 | 0.75 | 2,250 | 2,300 |
| 2 | Opus | 6,000 | 270,000 | 270,000 | 1.5 | 9,000 | 9,000 |
| 3 | Sonnet | 6,000 | 400,000 | 270,000 | 1.98 | 11,889 | 10,000 (ceiling) |

Check for #1: 3,000 × 0.75 = 2,250, rounded to nearest 100 = 2,300 (2,250 rounds up under round-half-up; state the rounding rule if this matters: 사용자 확인 필요).
Acceptance: a test passes if each row gives the cap above, and an overview file over its cap fails the check (measure with the project charcount).

## (e) Open questions for the user
1. ctx unit: tokens (as shown in the status line and T values) or characters? Overview cap is in chars, so the ratio needs one unit. 사용자 확인 필요
2. Direction: plan has cap growing with ctx (more context, longer overview allowed). Or should cap shrink as ctx grows (save tokens)? 사용자 확인 필요
3. FLOOR = 1,000 chars is my choice. Confirm or give a value. 사용자 확인 필요
4. Rounding rule (nearest 100, half up) and whether the 10,000 ceiling is per overview file. 사용자 확인 필요

# review: 261029-plan-parallel-load.md
date: 2026-10-29
verdict: run only after the changes below; as written, the verdict and the cap are not defensible.
scope: review only; plan not edited; claude not run.

1. (1) parallel check + load step: not enough as written
   - problem a: the prompt "Reply with the single word OK." is too short. Each call is mostly node startup + one short request, so wrapper intervals [start,end] overlap even if the server queues the requests. Overlap of process lifetimes proves 3 processes existed together. It does not prove the requests ran at the same time.
   - problem b: 2 rounds x 3 measures only concurrency 3. With no concurrency-1 reference there is nothing to compare, so it is a repeatability check, not a load measurement.
   - decision (minimum change):
     - add step 1a baseline: 2 solo calls (b1, b2), run one after the other, same command. b1 is also the auth check (see 4).
     - change the fixed prompt so the request takes real time: "Write the numbers 1 to 150 separated by single spaces. No other text." (about 450 output tokens, a few seconds on haiku; cost cents).
     - keep step 1 (3 parallel) and step 2 (2 rounds x 3). The load metric is then: median duration_api_ms at c=3 / median at c=1 (b1,b2). Report the ratio. Call it "load at c=3 vs c=1" only; do not claim a throughput curve.
     - total calls: 2 + 3 + 6 = 11.
   - parallel verdict rule (replaces line 31): all calls exit 0 AND is_error=false AND every pair of API intervals in the batch overlaps by >= 50% of the shorter one AND batch makespan (max t_result - min t_init) <= 0.6 x sum(duration_api_ms of the batch). Serialized: makespan >= 0.9 x sum. In between: report "부분 병렬 / 판정 보류" with the numbers.
   - optional for the load step: c=5 is not needed for the verdict and does not fit the fallback cap in (2). Leave it out.

2. (2) $2.50 ledger stop + $0.20 per call: does not hold $3 if the flag is ignored
   - problem: the ledger is checked only between batches. If --max-budget-usd is ignored under subscription login, nothing limits a single call. The plan's fallback "9 x 0.20 = $1.80" assumes the $0.20 cap holds, which is exactly the case being covered, so the argument is circular. The "cost field 0/absent" branch has the same flaw.
   - decision:
     - limit each call by its structure, not by the flag: add `--max-turns 1` and run without tools (`--tools ""` if `claude --help` or the docs list it; otherwise keep the no-tool prompt and record num_turns). One call = one model request.
     - per-call kill at 120 s wall clock (macOS has no `timeout`: `perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 env ... claude ...`).
     - exact fallback number: assumed worst case per in-flight call B = $0.60. Derivation (가정, Haiku 4.5 list prices, not in notes): 200k context x $2.00/M (1h cache write) = $0.40, plus 32k output x $5/M = $0.16, total $0.56, rounded up.
     - pre-launch rule (replaces the post-hoc 2.50 check): launch a batch of n only if ledger_sum + n x 0.60 <= 3.00. For n=3, ledger_sum must be <= $1.20. For n=1 (baselines), <= $2.40.
     - extra halt: any single call total_cost_usd > $0.20, or b1 cost > $0.10 (setup much heavier than assumed, e.g. MCP tool definitions loaded) -> stop and report.
     - total_cost_usd absent or 0 in b1 -> the ledger cannot work. Stop after step 1 (b1, b2 + 3 parallel = 5 calls; 5 x 0.60 = $3.00 worst case) and skip step 2.
     - keep `--max-budget-usd 0.20` as a secondary guard. If any call returns subtype error_max_budget_usd, record it as evidence that the flag is enforced.
     - expected spend: 11 calls x about $0.03-0.07 = about $0.3-0.8 (가정). The $1.20 gate should never be reached.

3. (3) fields to record (the verdict must not rest on start times alone)
   - decision: use `--output-format stream-json --verbose` and put one clock on each stdout line: `perl -MTime::HiRes=time -ne 'printf "%.3f %s", time, $_'`. Per call, record:
     - wrapper: t_launch (before exec), t_exit (after exit), pid (`$!`), exit code, stderr text.
     - stream timestamps: t_init (system/init line), t_first (first assistant line), t_result (result line). API interval = [t_init, t_result]. It excludes node startup and is used for overlap and makespan.
     - result fields: subtype, is_error, duration_ms, duration_api_ms, num_turns, session_id, total_cost_usd, usage.input_tokens, usage.output_tokens, usage.cache_creation_input_tokens, usage.cache_read_input_tokens, modelUsage keys (model ids).
     - init field: apiKeySource.
     - derived per batch: pairwise overlap (s) and overlap %, makespan, sum(duration_api_ms), peak concurrency from a sweep over the API intervals (not the wrapper intervals), ratio to median baseline.
   - field names (duration_api_ms, apiKeySource, init line shape) are 가정. Verify them on b1 output before step 1. If a name differs, map it and note the mapping in the result file. If there are no per-line timestamps from stream-json, fall back to the wrapper intervals and mark the verdict "추정".
   - distinct session_id and pid only prove separate sessions. They do not prove concurrency; do not use them as parallel evidence.
   - cache_read_input_tokens > 0 on later calls is evidence of a shared prompt cache. Record it; do not interpret cost differences.

4. (4) /tmp only + child env without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: yes, with fixes
   - decision /tmp: yes. Use `D=$(mktemp -d /tmp/plc.XXXXXX)` instead of a fixed /tmp/plc (no stale files), one subdir per call, and the ledger at $D/ledger.txt. Never use the repo as cwd. Notes:
     - macOS /tmp is /private/tmp. Session files still go to ~/.claude/projects/-private-tmp-plc-*. Add `--no-session-persistence` if --help lists it; otherwise record this side effect.
     - /tmp does not stop user-level loading: ~/.claude/settings.json hooks, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and claude.ai MCP connectors still load and add time and tokens. Add `--strict-mcp-config` (no --mcp-config) to load no MCP. In step 0, record the hook count in ~/.claude/settings.json (count only). If there are hooks, add `--setting-sources project` if --help lists it (auth is not stored in settings). Do not use --bare (DECISIONS: fails on subscription login).
   - decision env: yes, drop it, and make it consistent and checked:
     - fix the inconsistency: step 0.4 drops API_KEY + AUTH_TOKEN, but the step 1 command drops API_KEY only. Use one launcher script $D/run.sh for every call: `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN ...`.
     - step 0 check ($0): `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN /usr/bin/env | grep -c -E '^ANTHROPIC_(API_KEY|AUTH_TOKEN)='` must print 0.
     - stop (do not unset silently) if ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK or CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX is set: they change the provider or billing.
     - env -u does not cover apiKeyHelper. Step 0: `grep -c apiKeyHelper ~/.claude/settings.json` (count only). Nonzero -> stop.
     - auth check: b1 init apiKeySource must be "none" (가정 field). Any other value -> halt after b1, so at most 1 call is billed to the API. If `claude auth status` exists ($0), run it under the same env and record only the auth method.

5. other fixes
   - the step 1 command line still uses `date +%s.%N` (prints a literal N on macOS). Put the perl clock in the command itself so the executor does not copy the broken line.
   - stop conditions: add "exit 0 but is_error=true or subtype != success", and grep the rate-limit words in the result text too, not only in stderr.
   - order: step 0 -> b1 (auth + field check) -> b2 -> step 1 (3 parallel) -> gate -> step 2 round 1 -> gate -> round 2. Each gate = the pre-launch rule from (2) plus the stop conditions.
   - executor: haiku-runner is fine. Give it run.sh and the parser (one awk/python -I script in $D, not in the repo) so it does not improvise the overlap math.
   - result file: add columns t_init, t_result, duration_api_ms, cache_read_input_tokens, apiKeySource. Report the c=3/c=1 ratio and which pre-launch gate values were checked.

date: 2026-10-29
status: plan only (no claude command run, no source edited)
cap: total $3 hard; stop launching at ledger sum >= $2.50; per call --max-budget-usd 0.20
calls: 3 (parallel check) + 6 (load) = 9 max

## facts used (from notes)
- several Claude Code sessions can run at once: 확인됨 (code.claude.com model-config)
- `-p --output-format json` payload has `total_cost_usd`: 확인됨 (headless docs)
- `--max-budget-usd` is print-mode only; docs say "spend can pass the cap, leave headroom": 확인됨
- total_cost_usd is a client-side estimate, not billing: 확인됨
- shared prompt cache between concurrent sessions: 확인 안 됨
- budget flag behavior under subscription login: 확인 안 됨 (third-party report only) -> 가정
- local `claude --help` showing the flag: 확인 안 됨 -> check in step 0
- json field names for duration (e.g. duration_ms), exit/result subtype: 가정, verify on first output

## step 0 pre-check (no model call, $0)
1. Test shell: for each of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX: print name + set/unset only (`[ -n "${VAR+x}" ]`), never values.
2. `claude --version` must exit 0. Record version (budget cap enforcement needs v2.1.217+ per docs).
3. `claude --help | grep -i budget` : record whether flag listed (docs say help may omit flags; absence is not a blocker).
4. Child env for all calls: `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN claude ...` (so the run uses subscription login, not API billing).
Stop if: version fails, or key var cannot be removed from child env.

## step 1 parallel check (3 calls)
- Setup: `mkdir -p /tmp/plc/run1/c{1,2,3}` ; cwd per call = own dir (not the repo). Logs in /tmp/plc/run1/.
- Prompt (one line, fixed): "Reply with the single word OK."
- Launch all 3 in background within the same second:
  `(cd /tmp/plc/run1/cN && date +%s.%N > start; env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY claude -p "Reply with the single word OK." --model haiku --output-format json --max-budget-usd 0.20 > out.json 2> err.txt; echo $? > exit; date +%s.%N > end) &` then `wait`.
  (macOS date lacks %N: use `python3 -c 'import time;print(time.time())'` or `perl -MTime::HiRes=time -e 'print time'`.)
- Record per call: start, end, exit code, total_cost_usd, duration, stderr text.
- Parallel verdict rule: all 3 exit 0 AND time intervals overlap (max(start) < min(end)). Serialized if intervals are back-to-back (each start ~ previous end) or wall time ~ sum of durations. Fail if any non-zero exit.
- Ledger check after step 1: if sum >= $2.50 or any stop condition, halt (expected sum well under $0.30; 가정).

## step 2 load (2 rounds x 3 = 6 calls)
- Same command, same fixed prompt, dirs /tmp/plc/run2/r{1,2}c{1,2,3}.
- Round 1: launch 3, wait. Check ledger + stop conditions. Round 2: launch 3 only if ledger < $2.50 and no stop condition.
- Per call collect: total_cost_usd, duration (json duration field if present; else wall end-start), exit code.
- Max concurrency observed: sweep over all start/end timestamps (+1 at start, -1 at end), take the peak. Expected 3; <3 means serialization/throttling.
- Cache note: identical prompts may share cache across calls (확인 안 됨); cost variance between calls is not evidence either way.

## step 3 budget ledger (hard)
- Ledger file /tmp/plc/ledger.txt: one `callid cost` line per finished call; sum with awk after every batch.
- Rules: per-call `--max-budget-usd 0.20`; no new launch when sum >= 2.50; worst case in flight at stop = 3 calls x (0.20 + overshoot). Cap can be exceeded per call (docs), so 2.50 threshold leaves $0.50 headroom for 3 in-flight calls (overshoot assumed < $0.30 each... 가정).
- Enforcement of `--max-budget-usd` on subscription login: 가정 until checked. Check: after step 1, if any call cost > 0.20 or json shows subtype error_max_budget_usd, record it; if cost field is 0/absent under subscription, the ledger cannot enforce -> fall back to call-count cap (9 calls x 0.20 = $1.80 worst case, within $3) and report.
- total_cost_usd is a client estimate; real subscription usage is not measured (note in verdict).

## step 4 output
File: /Users/leekwangseok/PycharmProjects/claude-harness/notes/runs/261029-result-parallel-load.md
- Table: call id | start | end | cost (total_cost_usd) | exit code | parallel with which
- Sum of costs, max concurrency, wall time per round, version, env var status (set/unset only).
- Verdict: parallel works / not, with reason (overlap + all exit 0 + concurrency peak). State separately: evidence vs inference; unverified items (cache sharing, budget enforcement under subscription).

## stop conditions (halt, no further launches, write result with partial table)
- any non-zero exit code
- any rate-limit text in stderr/json (e.g. "rate limit", "429", "usage limit", "overloaded")
- ledger sum >= $2.50 (or the cap logic above reached)
- any step-0 failure

## blockers / open
- none known for planning. Needs main thread to run (this agent must not run claude); suggest haiku-runner executes steps 0-4.
- open: duration/field names in json unverified; subscription behavior of the budget flag unverified.

# review: 261029-plan-router-3tier.md
reviewer: opus-architect (design review, improvements only; plan/policy files not edited)
verdict: plan sound in structure (1 file, 6 units, size derived for metrics); 3 corrections required before implementation: sonnet tier = direct delegation (not plan+review), tests are NOT "args only", tag definitions dropped 3 old large items.

## decisions

1. sonnet tier behavior -> (a) direct: Haiku delegates to sonnet-analyst in one foreground round, no Haiku plan, no review step. Reject plan's proposal (b).
   - cost basis (261029-analysis-per-prompt-classify.md): classify call itself is a few % of main cost; real cost is in what the route triggers. Neither option switches the main session (main stays Haiku, pickModel unchanged), so the 8.5만 transition cost does not apply; the difference is hop count only.
   - (b) = Haiku plan write (Haiku main context grows toward 80k rotation) + sonnet-analyst review (reads plan + same files) + Haiku merge + Haiku agents execute + sonnet-reviewer = >=2 Sonnet calls + 3 Haiku steps. (a) = 1 sonnet-analyst call; it already hands mechanical sub-steps to Haiku (CLAUDE.md:11) and does not read files itself (DECISIONS:39).
   - for analysis/review/comparison tasks the plan IS the deliverable: (b) does the work twice (Haiku draft, Sonnet critique). planHint's review-only design exists to keep Opus (expensive) from executing; Sonnet as executor costs the same class as Sonnet as reviewer, so the restriction buys nothing.
   - safety: analysis says under-classification (design work routed low) is the expensive direction. (a) keeps sonnet-analyst's scope-first ESCALATE (CLAUDE.md:9) -> mis-tiered opus work gets escalated. In (b) review mode sonnet-analyst only writes improvements and never escalates -> no safety net.
   - sonnetHint wording (new const, classifier.go): "[routing: sonnet tier. Do not write a plan. In ONE foreground round delegate to sonnet-analyst: user's words quoted + target paths + 'reply: Korean 존댓말'. If it returns ESCALATE: <path>, give that path to opus-architect as is (no Haiku plan step). sonnet-reviewer only before release/merge/submission.]\n"
   - TestSonnetTierHint: contains "sonnet-analyst", "ESCALATE", "opus-architect"; does NOT contain "plan-<topic>" or "write the full design"; sonnet tier task has sonnetHint prefix and not planHint; haiku tier has neither.

2. opus tier -> keep existing plan->review->merge workflow (planHint), not opus-architect direct.
   - reason: it is the user's standing decision (DECISIONS:38, CLAUDE.md:32 "Opus is for design only ... Opus/Sonnet do not execute"); changing it is outside this plan's 비목표 and needs a separate user decision. Cost: Opus reads Haiku's plan + needed files and outputs improvements only (short Opus output, the 5x-priced part) instead of a full plan.
   - refinement A: opus tier review = opus-architect only. Drop "and/or sonnet-analyst" from planHint step (2): sonnet-level work now has its own tier, so a second reviewer is double cost. TestHaikuPlanWorkflow :136 list then checks "opus-architect", "notes/runs/", "Haiku agents" (remove "sonnet-analyst" from that list, or keep it only if planHint keeps the "and/or").
   - refinement B: rename planHint prefix "[routing: large or judgment task." -> "[routing: opus tier (design/judgment)." so CLAUDE.md hint name, metrics `tier`, and hint text agree.
   - exception (no new code): an ESCALATE path from sonnet-analyst already is a scope file -> goes to opus-architect directly (per CLAUDE.md:9), skipping the Haiku plan step. Covered by sonnetHint text above.

3. missing/invalid tag default -> confirm sonnet. Also confirm "unsure -> sonnet" for both haiku/sonnet and sonnet/opus boundaries.
   - evidence: production classifier is Sonnet (conductorModel); 30/30 correct, 0 parse failures (261029-test-router-30-prod-args.md). Haiku-model errors were all small->large (over-escalation), 0 large->small (261029-test-effort-haiku-vs-sonnet.md:53). Missing tag is rare and observed bias is upward, so defaulting to opus would pay an Opus review on every parse failure for little gain.
   - the expensive under-classification case is covered by decision 1's ESCALATE path; this is the condition that makes sonnet default safe. If decision 1 were (b), default should be opus instead.
   - keep the explicit opus trigger list in classifyPrompt (design/architecture, trade-off/recommendation, strategy/priority/roadmap, unknown-cause diagnosis, repeated failure, 'opus로') so "unsure" stays narrow.
   - missing from plan's new definitions (old large list items with no new home) -> add:
     - version bump with exact text, identical-wording replacement -> haiku (matches CLAUDE.md:9 haiku-coder rule; resolves P3 label conflict).
     - release, deploy, merge -> sonnet (needs sonnet-reviewer; not design).
     - new feature or refactor -> sonnet when scope is given; opus when the design is undecided.
     - classifyPrompt :22 "A lookup or edit that is small is sent straight to a Haiku session" -> "...that is tier haiku...".
   - parse: if both `tier:` and old `size:` present, tier wins; size-only -> small=haiku, large=sonnet, SizeDefaulted=true (as plan says).

4. policy -> append a new line to notes/DECISIONS.md; do not edit line 38. Confirmed: header says "One line each. Newest at bottom." and existing entries supersede by new lines (e.g. [conductor] "Supersedes conductor-session rule").
   - suggested line: "- [routing] 261029 user: <user's words verbatim> -> classifier tags tier haiku|sonnet|opus (size kept as derived metric: haiku=small, sonnet|opus=large). haiku: Haiku agents direct; sonnet: Haiku delegates directly to sonnet-analyst (no plan; ESCALATE -> opus-architect); opus: planHint workflow (Haiku plan -> opus-architect review -> merge -> Haiku agents).    - non-policy text the plan missed (code, same commit, no approval needed): repl.go:898 flag help "a one-shot Sonnet classifier tags size and adds the plan->review->execute hint to large tasks" -> "tags tier (haiku|sonnet|opus); sonnet tier -> sonnet-analyst hint, opus tier -> plan->review->execute hint"; repl.go:60 comment "large work:" -> "opus-tier work:"; classifier.go :30-31 planHint comment "large task" -> "opus-tier task".

# review: plan-router-classifier (read-only)
target: notes/runs/261029-plan-router-classifier.md
checked: internal/harness/classifier.go (parseRouteFull :65, pickModel :38, route :138, classify :109), internal/harness/conductor_test.go

## concrete issues
1. test break: conductor_test.go:14 bad-list has "topic: same\ntask: x" expecting ok=false. Plan change 3 (missing size -> large, ok=true) makes it ok=true, so TestParseRoute fails. Plan step 5 does not mention this line. Fix: move that case to an ok-case (size large) or drop it from bad list.
2. planHint blast radius: classifier.go:94 attaches planHint when model=haiku && size=large. Missing or garbled size (e.g. "Small.", "medium") now gets full plan workflow (Haiku plan + opus-architect/sonnet-analyst round). Cost/latency caller: every haiku-main prompt with bad tag.
3. forced opus caller: pickModel :43 delegates only when size=="small". Missing size now -> no delegate, so unrelated side tasks run in Opus main context (no rotation). Add test: topic new, no size, cur opus -> opus, delegate=false (documented, intended?).
4. silent drift: route() :147-163 logs no size and routeResult (:54-56) has no Size field. Cannot count how often default-to-large fires, and no before/after baseline. Add Size to routeResult, log f["size"] and f["size_defaulted"]=true.
5. parse edge: value is lowercased then compared exactly. "small." or "small " currently fails (ok=false); after change it silently becomes large. Either normalize (trim ". ") or accept the drift via metric in item 4.
6. prompt-test coupling: conductor_test.go:64-65 asserts substrings "topic: same|new" and "size: small|large". Keep these literals verbatim when editing classifyPrompt (:15-22). Plan step 5 keyword asserts are brittle; assert only "size: small|large" and the "unsure" rule text.
7. docs: plan has no step for docs. CLAUDE.md:31, DECISIONS.md:32,38 describe size tagging and pickModel/planHint behavior. Update if default-to-large is adopted.

## ordering
- add step 0: run baseline `go test ./internal/harness -run 'TestParseRoute|TestMainRouteSwitchPolicy|TestHaikuPlanWorkflow'` before edits.
- order: parse change + test line 14 fix together (else step 6 fails); prompt text edit after; metric (item 4) before any measurement claim.

## test gaps
- no live size assertion: TestClassifierLive (conductor_test.go:22-41) checks model only; routeResult has no size. Add size or planHint check on the misrouted prompts (costs ~$0.007 each, CHAUDE_LIVE=1).
- no test for missing-size on haiku main (planHint expected) or missing-task/topic still ok=false beyond existing "topic: new\nsize: small" case.
- no test that kind default stays "other" when size missing (plan says keep; add one case).

## kept as-is (checked)
- ok=false for missing topic/task: already covered (conductor_test.go:14).
- worker assignment (:98-104) independent of size: edit-size change does not drop worker reuse.
- classify parse failure returns os.ErrInvalid (:130-131), route returns raw line: unchanged by plan.

# plan: router classifier misrouting (large tagged small)
goal: fewer large/judgment tasks tagged size:small (which skips design step)
constraint: model stays Sonnet; only prompt text + parsing if needed; do not commit

## evidence (haiku-scout)
- classifyPrompt: internal/harness/classifier.go:15-22; size rule: "small = single-file or mechanical edits, lookup, search, count, run/monitor, short explanation, small fix. large = multi-file or multi-step changes, design/architecture, hard diagnosis, weighing trade-offs, judgment calls, strategy/priority/roadmap, 'opus로', repeated failure."
- no "when unsure" rule for size (only topic has "When unsure, same")
- parseRouteFull :65: ok=false if size not small|large; kind missing -> other silently; classify returns os.ErrInvalid on parse fail (:130); route() logs metrics error and passes raw line, no switch
- planHint :31-33 attached :94-95 when model haiku && size large
- tests: conductor_test.go (TestParseRoute :9, TestMainRouteSwitchPolicy :44, TestHaikuPlanWorkflow :71). No test for missing-tag fallback.

## changes
1. classifyPrompt size rule: add explicit large signals: multi-file change; design/architecture question; release/deploy/version bump/merge; ambiguous or open-ended scope; multi-step plan; trade-off/comparison/recommendation; new feature; refactor; diagnosis with unknown cause.
2. Add rule: "size: when unsure between small and large, large." Define small narrowly: only if single file/one-step AND clear scope.
3. Parsing: size tag missing/invalid currently -> ok=false (no routing). Decide: keep ok=false for missing topic/task, but for missing/invalid size alone default to large (safe side) rather than failing. Keep kind default other.
4. planHint text: keep wording; no change unless review finds issue.
5. Tests (conductor_test.go): 
   - classifyPrompt contains new signal keywords and "unsure" rule
   - parseRouteFull: missing size -> ok with large (new behavior); invalid size value -> large; missing topic -> ok=false; missing task -> ok=false; missing kind -> other
   - size large + haiku current -> planHint appended (existing coverage check)
6. Verify: go build ./... ; go test ./... ; sonnet-reviewer on diff.

## risks
- over-large routing raises cost (Opus/plan workflow for trivial tasks); mitigate by keeping small examples explicit
- defaulting missing size to large changes ok semantics; ensure callers (pickModel) handle it

## merged from review (final spec)
0. baseline: go test ./internal/harness -run 'TestParseRoute|TestMainRouteSwitchPolicy|TestHaikuPlanWorkflow' before edits
A. parseRouteFull: normalize size value (trim spaces and trailing "."); missing/invalid size -> "large" with ok=true (topic/task still required). Update conductor_test.go:14 bad case "topic: same\ntask: x" -> move to ok case expecting large.
B. classifyPrompt: keep literals "topic: same|new" and "size: small|large" verbatim; add large signals + "when unsure between small and large, large" + narrow small definition.
C. routeResult gets Size field; route() metrics log size and size_defaulted=true when defaulted.
D. tests: missing size -> large + kind other; "Small." -> small; "medium" -> large; missing topic / missing task -> ok=false; pickModel topic new, no size, cur opus -> opus, delegate=false; haiku main + missing size -> planHint appended; prompt asserts only "size: small|large" and the unsure rule text.
E. docs (CLAUDE.md:31, DECISIONS.md:32,38) NOT edited (out of scope); flagged as follow-up.
F. live test size assertion skipped (costs API); flagged.

# review: 261029-plan-router-context-split.md
date: 2026-10-29
reviewer: opus-architect
scope: improvements only; plan not edited; no source change

## new evidence (gathered for this review, 0 API calls)
- E1 neither earlier test used production args. test-sonnet-vs-haiku (/tmp/router-test.wLXJCF/run_one.sh): router prompt in user msg, default system prompt, default tools, --max-turns 1, --strict-mcp-config. test-injection F: same + CLAUDE.md in user msg. production classify() (classifier.go:122-125): --system-prompt classifyPrompt, --tools "", no --max-turns, no --strict-mcp-config, cwd os.TempDir(), cleanEnv(0).
- E2 haiku F failure modes (error_max_turns = tried to use tools; prose answer) both need tools or the default system prompt. Production has neither, so the F result says nothing about production Haiku.
- E3 CLAUDE.md reach (A1): no ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md; no CLAUDE.md in $TMPDIR (/var/folders/rb/.../T/) or its parents (/var/folders, /var). Project CLAUDE.md cannot reach the router through the files on disk.
- E4 production classify metrics (notes/metrics/*.jsonl, stage=classify, n=103, errors 0): result_ctx median 19,602 tokens (cache_read median 18,519, cache_creation median 1,108); cost_usd median $0.0079, mean $0.0254 (outliers up to 174k ctx / $0.132 on 10-28, cause unknown). classifyPrompt ~3.7k chars plus input is ~1-2k tokens, so about 17-18k tokens per call come from somewhere else even with --system-prompt and --tools "".
- E5 ~/.claude/settings.json: hooks {} , mcpServers none, enabledPlugins = pyright-lsp, session-report, serena. Plugins can add MCP tools (serena), hooks, skills. These are the likely source of E4, not CLAUDE.md.
- E6 claude 2.1.312 --help: --setting-sources (user,project,local), --disable-slash-commands, --strict-mcp-config, --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections exist; --max-turns is not listed but works (earlier tests got error_max_turns). --bare needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (OAuth never read) -> do NOT use; it conflicts with cleanEnv (billing).
- E7 plan cost estimate is off: production Sonnet router ~$0.008/call (E4), not $0.05. The $0.05 came from the test setup with default tools.

## decisions
1. (1) split work: defer U1 (isolation flags, MkdirTemp). The CLAUDE.md part is not needed: A1 holds by code (E1) and by disk (E3). First step = Step 0 baseline: 30 samples x {sonnet, haiku} with exact production classify() arguments. Keep U1 only as a conditional step, justified by the ~18k-token unexplained context (E4), not by CLAUDE.md. Run U1 only if Step 0b (below) shows a flag removes most of that context. Even if Haiku is not adopted it may still be worth doing: cache_read 18.5k x $0.30/M ~ $0.0056 = ~70% of the Sonnet router cost per call. After U1, re-run the same 30 x 2 with the U1 args.
   - how to guarantee identical args: replace U4 (shell script copying the args, which will drift) with a Go live test that calls classify() itself, e.g. internal/harness/router_eval_test.go TestRouterEval, gated CHAUDE_LIVE=1, reading the frozen eval set and writing a results jsonl to notes/runs/. Only prerequisite: router model selectable without changing defaults = do U2 first (routerModel(), env CHAUDE_ROUTER_MODEL, default "sonnet"). U2 is the only code change before Step 0.
   - eval set format must carry per sample: id, cur (current session model), lastUser (previous prompt, can be ""), prompt, expected size, expected kind; cands nil. Without lastUser/cur, the plan's input differs from production in.
2. (2) minimum conditions:
   - P-S: production args, sonnet, 30 prompts, 1 run (~$0.25).
   - P-H: production args, haiku, 30 prompts, 3 runs (~$0.2 total). Repeats are cheap and give the only variance signal; score per prompt by majority, and also report how many prompts were 3/3 consistent.
   - M control: no new calls. Compare P-H on the P1-P10 subset with the existing haiku M 8/10 and sonnet M 10/10 (test-injection file). Run M-haiku x30 (~$0.09) only if P-H fails the gate, to tell whether the cause is prompt placement (system vs user msg, A4) or the model's limit.
   - drop condition F entirely (not a production path, E2).
   - Step 0b (leak attribution, ~4 haiku calls): 1 call with production args + --output-format stream-json --verbose and read the init event (tools, mcp_servers, slash_commands/skills, plugins). Then 1 call each adding --strict-mcp-config, --setting-sources "", --disable-slash-commands. Record result ctx for each.
   - budget: cap $1.00 (was $2.50); stop on cumulative total_cost_usd.
3. (3) threshold: "Haiku >= 2 of 30 below Sonnet -> keep Sonnet" is not justified as the only gate. At n=30 one run, 28/30 has a 95% CI of about 78-99%, so a 1-2 point gap is noise and the rule ignores which direction the error goes. Replace with (all must hold to switch; else Sonnet stays, U2 default unchanged):
   - a. under-routing (expected large -> Haiku small, majority vote) = 0. This is the harmful direction: a large task skips planHint. Earlier Haiku errors (P3, P7) were all small->large, which only costs plan overhead.
   - b. size accuracy, majority vote: Haiku >= Sonnet - 1.
   - c. consistency: >= 27/30 prompts with the same Haiku size in 3/3 runs.
   - d. parse failures <= 1 across 90 Haiku calls (production fails open: classify err -> line sent unrouted, route() returns line), and each one is counted as wrong in b.
   - kind accuracy and topic: report only, not a gate. kind matters only for the worker pick on small edit. topic only changes the result when cur=opus (pickModel).
   - third rollback rule (U1 vs "9-10/10 earlier"): change the baseline to the Step 0 P-S result. The 10-sample number came from non-production args.
   - the final switch stays a user decision (open question 1). A pass only makes the switch allowed.
4. (4) verify A1 and A2 first, in this order:
   - A1 (CLAUDE.md does not reach the router): already supported at 0 cost (E1 code, E3 disk). Closing check, no extra call: in Step 0, router result_ctx with production args should stay around 19.6k (E4). Adding a test CLAUDE.md copy to $TMPDIR is not needed. The TestClassifyArgs check that the args contain no CLAUDE.md string is enough as a regression guard.
   - A2 (global settings/plugins inject context into -p): reword the assumption to "enabled plugins (serena MCP, session-report, pyright-lsp) and skills listing add ~17-18k tokens" (E4, E5). Verify with Step 0b: the init event lists what is loaded, then measure which single flag drops result_ctx toward ~2k. Also check that --setting-sources "" still authenticates through OAuth/keychain and does not change the model or env settings (rc 0, same `model` in the result json).
   - A4 is answered by Step 0 itself (P-H vs existing M on P1-P10). A5 should be reworded: the CLAUDE.md cause is already ruled out for production, so the question is now "Haiku limit vs plugin/skills noise", answered by P-H before and after U1. A6 (--max-turns 1) is moot with --tools "": do not add the flag in the baseline.

## other improvements
- order: U2 -> eval set frozen -> Step 0b -> Step 0 (P-S, P-H) -> decide U1 -> (U1 + U3 + re-run) -> user decision. U3 depends on U1's buildRouterArgs(); if U1 is skipped, U3 shrinks to testing that classify() still uses --system-prompt and --tools "" (still needs a small args builder).
- U1 MkdirTemp per call: low value (E3); if kept, reuse one dir per process, not one per call (latency and cleanup on crash).
- 30-sample source (open question 2): metrics rows do not include prompt text, so the new 20 must be written by hand or taken from the transcripts. Keep small:large 15:15, and include >= 5 large prompts that sound small (short wording, multi-file effect). These test the gate in 3a.
- record per call: model, run#, size, kind, topic, parse ok, cost, result_ctx, duration_ms. The results table should separate sonnet and haiku cost (the plan mixes them).
- outlier rows on 10-28 (ctx 174k, $0.132): find out if they are pre-`--tools ""` code before using mean cost anywhere; use the median.

# 계획: 라우터 컨텍스트 분리 (Haiku 라우터에 최소 컨텍스트)
date: 2026-10-29
status: 계획만. 소스 수정 없음.

## 목표
- 라우터 호출이 받는 텍스트를 고정 프롬프트 + 사용자 프롬프트 + 짧은 세션 메모로 한정한다.
- CLAUDE.md(8005자), 시스템 규칙(약 885자), 훅 주입이 라우터에 닿지 않음을 코드와 실측으로 보장한다.
- 이 상태에서 Haiku 라우터가 Sonnet 수준 정확도를 내는지 확인한다.

## 현재 흐름
근거(evidence):
- classifier.go:14-24 classifyPrompt가 라우터 고정 프롬프트. classifier.go:122-123 에서 `--system-prompt classifyPrompt`, `--tools ""`, `--no-session-persistence`로 전달.
- classifier.go:117-121 user 메시지 = 현재 모델 + 직전 프롬프트(200자) + 워커 후보 + 사용자 프롬프트(= "짧은 세션 메모" 역할).
- classifier.go:125 cmd.Dir = os.TempDir() → 프로젝트 CLAUDE.md 미로드 의도.
- classifier.go:14 conductorModel = "sonnet". 현재 운영 라우터는 Sonnet.
- 시스템 규칙 append(repl.go:184-191)는 메인 세션 args에만 있고 classify()에는 없음.
- 주입 인벤토리(261029-explore-prompt-injection-inventory.md): CLAUDE.md, 시스템 규칙, 훅은 메인 호출 기준 기록.
- 테스트(261029-test-router-injection-minimal-vs-full.md): F 조건 = CLAUDE.md를 user 메시지에 직접 붙임(Haiku 3/10, 파싱 실패 6). M 조건 8/10, Sonnet M 10/10, F 9/10.
추론(inference, 미검증):
- 테스트 F 조건은 운영 classify()와 같지 않다. 운영 코드는 이미 CLAUDE.md를 직접 붙이지 않는다. 따라서 "실제 흐름에서 Haiku가 풀 컨텍스트를 받는다"는 점은 코드상 확인되지 않았다.
- 남는 누출 후보: (a) 사용자 전역 설정(~/.claude/settings.json)의 훅·MCP·플러그인이 -p 호출에도 로드, (b) Claude Code 기본 도구/컨텍스트 오버헤드(테스트 M에서도 호출당 cache_creation 약 12k 토큰), (c) TempDir 안에 CLAUDE.md가 생길 가능성.
- 테스트 M은 라우터 프롬프트를 user 메시지로 줬고 운영은 system prompt로 준다. 둘은 동일 조건이 아니다.

## 분리 설계
라우터 호출 규약(한 곳에서만 정의):
- system: classifyPrompt 그대로(`--system-prompt`로 기본 시스템 프롬프트 대체).
- user: 현재 모델, 직전 프롬프트 200자, 후보, 사용자 프롬프트. 추가 텍스트 없음.
- 격리 플래그: `--tools ""`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--setting-sources ""`(훅·사용자 설정 차단), `--disable-slash-commands`, `--max-turns 1`, `--no-session-persistence`.
- cwd: 호출마다 빈 임시 디렉터리(os.MkdirTemp), 종료 후 삭제.
- 모델: 상수 대신 설정값(기본 현 정책 유지 = sonnet). Haiku 전환은 검증 통과 후 결정.
- 보호장치: 호출 직전 입력 길이 상한 검사(고정 프롬프트 + 입력이 예상 범위를 넘으면 로그).

## 변경 파일과 함수 (유닛당 파일 1개, 함수 1개)
1. U1 internal/harness/classifier.go · classify(): 격리 플래그 추가, cwd를 빈 임시 디렉터리로 교체.
2. U2 internal/harness/classifier.go · routerModel() 신설: conductorModel 상수 대신 환경/설정에서 읽고 기본값 sonnet.
3. U3 internal/harness/classifier_test.go(신규) · TestClassifyArgs: 인자 구성(플래그, system prompt 사용, CLAUDE.md 문자열 미포함)을 실행 없이 검사. 이를 위해 인자 생성부를 buildRouterArgs()로 분리하는 것은 U1에 포함.
4. U4 scripts/router-eval.sh(신규) · 30샘플 비교 드라이버. 운영 인자 구성과 동일하게 호출.
- 의존: U1 → U3, U4. U2는 독립. 5개 미만 파일.

## 검증
30샘플 테스트(호출 전에 고정):
- 프롬프트 30개와 기대 size(small/large), kind를 호출 전에 notes/runs/261029-router-eval-set.md에 확정·기록. 이전 10개(P1-P10) 포함, 20개 신규. small/large 15:15.
- 기대값은 사용자 판단 기준. 이전 "version bump" 같은 애매 항목은 분류기 규칙(large) 기준으로 확정 후 기록, 이후 수정 금지.
- 모델 2종(Sonnet, Haiku)을 모두 분리 컨텍스트(U1 인자)로 각 30회 호출, 총 60회. 반복 없음(분산 미측정을 결과에 명시).
- 예상 비용: 이전 평균 Sonnet 약 $0.05, Haiku 약 $0.003/호출 → 약 $1.6. 상한 $2.50, 누적이 넘으면 중단.
- 측정: size 정확도, kind 정확도, 파싱 실패 수, 호출당 비용, usage(cache_creation).
- 누출 점검: 호출 1건의 입력 토큰 수를 고정 프롬프트 + 입력 추정치와 비교, 훅 실행 로그 없음 확인.

## 가정
- A1 운영 classify()는 이미 CLAUDE.md를 받지 않는다. 확인: 임시 디렉터리 cwd로 호출 후 응답/usage에서 CLAUDE.md 문구 유무, 또는 입력 토큰 비교.
- A2 사용자 전역 설정이 -p 호출에 훅·MCP를 싣는다. 확인: `--setting-sources ""` 유무로 입력 토큰 차이 측정.
- A3 `--setting-sources`, `--disable-slash-commands`가 현 claude 2.1.312에 존재한다. 확인: `claude --help`.
- A4 system prompt 방식(운영)이 user 메시지 방식(테스트 M)보다 Haiku 정확도에 불리하지 않다. 확인: 30샘플에서 운영 방식으로 측정(테스트 M 8/10과 비교).
- A5 Haiku 실패 원인은 CLAUDE.md이고 모델 한계가 아니다. 확인: 분리 컨텍스트 Haiku 파싱 실패 0이면 지지.
- A6 `--max-turns 1`이 분리 컨텍스트에서 정상 응답을 막지 않는다. 확인: 파싱 실패 수.

## 롤백 조건
- Haiku 분리 정확도가 Sonnet 분리 정확도보다 30개 중 2개 이상 낮으면 라우터는 Sonnet 유지(U2 기본값 그대로, 변경 없음).
- 파싱 실패가 Haiku에서 1건이라도 있으면 보고하고 해당 건을 오답 처리.
- U1 격리 플래그가 Sonnet 정확도를 기존(10샘플 기준 9-10/10 수준)보다 떨어뜨리면 U1만 되돌림(git revert 단위: classifier.go).

## 열린 질문 (사용자 결정)
- 라우터 모델 정책을 바꿀지 여부: 검증 후 Haiku가 기준을 충족해도 비용 절감(호출당 약 $0.05 → $0.003)을 취할지, Sonnet을 유지할지.
- 30샘플 중 신규 20개의 출처: 실제 사용 로그(notes/metrics)에서 뽑을지 새로 작성할지.
- 격리 플래그가 사용자 전역 훅을 막아도 괜찮은지(라우터에 한정되므로 영향 없다고 추론, 확인 필요).

=== notes/runs/261029-plan-router-haiku-policy-review.md (mtime 2026-10-29) ===
# review: 261029-plan-router-haiku-policy.md
date: 2026-10-29
reviewer: opus-architect (design review only; plan/policy files not edited, nothing implemented)
verdict: plan direction OK; change the pass gates, eval set size, tie-break, rollback prompt coupling, and step order as below.

1. Gate 1 (zero non-haiku sent to haiku): keep it as a hard gate, but count it correctly.
   - why keep: the costs are lopsided. A leak sends design or multi-file work to a Haiku session with no plan/sonnet hint, so the answer is wrong. Over-classifying only costs money, and the planHint/sonnetHint path absorbs it.
   - unit: count distinct prompts, not calls. If any of the 3 runs routes a non-haiku prompt to haiku, that prompt counts as a leak. The 3 calls on one prompt are correlated, so 300 calls do not show a 1% bound.
   - what a 0 means (rule of three, 95% upper bound per prompt is about 3/n): plan's 50 non-haiku prompts -> 0 leaks only shows <=6%. 100 distinct non-haiku -> <=3%. Decision: at least 100 distinct non-haiku prompts.
   - label noise: boundary items between haiku and sonnet get the label sonnet (same as the tie-break) and stay in gate 1. Pre-marked boundary items are capped at 10% of the set. Labels must not change after any model call. If the Sonnet baseline also routes an item to haiku, report it, but it still counts.
   - add as a reference metric (not a gate): the same leak count for the Sonnet baseline. If Sonnet also leaks, the label or the rule set is the problem, not Haiku.

2. Gate 2 (tier accuracy within 2%p of Sonnet): sample per tier.
   - problem: with 100 prompts, 1 prompt = 1%p and the binomial SE at about 97% is about 1.7%p, so a 2%p gap cannot be resolved. With sonnet at 20 (plan) or 4 (old set), the sonnet tier is mostly guesswork.
   - decision: eval set of 150 prompts, haiku 50 / sonnet 50 / opus 50. Absolute floor is 30 per tier (1 error = 3.3%p). The 50 is chosen so that 1 error = 2%p.
   - drop the "50 fixed + 50 보조" split. All prompts are labeled, frozen and scored. Zero overlap with the old 30-sample set (it becomes the dev set, see 3).
   - gate, count-based and paired on the same prompts:
     a. overall: Haiku errors (mean of the 3 runs) <= Sonnet errors + 2%p of 150 (= 3 prompts).
     b. per tier: Haiku errors in that tier (run mean) <= Sonnet errors in that tier + 2 prompts (4%p of 50). This stops a weak sonnet tier from hiding inside the overall average.
     c. opus->sonnet under-classification (the other quality-losing direction) <= Sonnet baseline + 2 prompts.
   - Sonnet baseline: 1 run, as in the plan. Its run-to-run noise is accepted. Report it as a reference metric.
   - cost check: Sonnet 150 x ~$0.0045 = ~$0.68; Haiku new prompt 450 x ~$0.0003 = ~$0.14; extra arm in item 3 adds ~$0.14; total ~$1.0, under the $3 cap.
   - consistency gate 3 (>=90% of prompts with the same tier in all 3 runs) stays, computed over the 150 prompts.

3. Prompt tuning: constraints, and order relative to the test set.
   order (decision: tune first, then fix the test set):
     a. tune only on the dev set = old 30 prompts (notes/runs/261029-haiku-router-30-samples-list.md), Haiku 3 runs per draft.
     b. freeze the prompt: record its sha256 in the test file header. No edits after this point.
     c. a separate agent (haiku-drafter, fresh instance) writes the 150-prompt test set and labels. It sees only the tier definitions in this review/plan and never the prompt text, so it cannot write easy prompts that just match keywords.
     d. one run. No re-tuning against test results. If the run fails: roll back. Any later re-tune needs a new test set (at least the failed tier's 50 replaced).
   the new prompt must keep:
     - output: exactly 5 lines in the order topic/tier/kind/worker/task; fixed values only; "nothing else". Keep "Always output topic, tier, kind and worker."
     - every semantic rule of the current tier lists, with no silent drops. The plan's draft drops these, and they must come back: "version bump with exact text" (haiku), "one-step edit of one file with a clear scope" (haiku), "clear multi-step task" and "comparison summary" (sonnet), "new feature or refactor with a given scope" -> sonnet vs "whose design is open" -> opus, "repeated failure", "'opus로'". Add a table of old phrase -> new phrase to the test file.
     - no-match default = sonnet, never haiku. Haiku only on an explicit haiku-rule match. The draft's "first match, opus->sonnet->haiku" leaves no-match undefined, which is a leak risk.
     - tie-break: keep the current semantics exactly: "unsure haiku/sonnet -> sonnet; unsure sonnet/opus -> sonnet". Decision: do NOT adopt the draft's "always higher". It changes sonnet/opus routing (more opus = Haiku plan + Opus review rounds) and mixes a second variable into the model test. Safety only needs "unsure -> never haiku", which the current rule already gives.
     - topic: "When unsure, same." plus the existing new/same definitions.
     - kind/worker: keep "A lookup or edit that is tier haiku is sent straight to a Haiku session" and "worker only for kind edit, else new". Fix only the missing space in "session.worker:".
     - task suffix: 'reply: Korean 존댓말, ... before replying' byte-exact.
     - examples: one per tier, Korean, typical cases (not boundary), new sentences not in the dev or test set.
     - rules in English, Korean trigger words included in brackets (설계, 트레이드오프, 추천, 전략, 원인, 계획, 'opus로'), because inputs are Korean.
     - length: the -30% target is a reference metric, not a gate. Saving ~150 tokens on a ~$0.0003 Haiku call is negligible. Never cut a rule to hit the length.
   - add test arm (c): Haiku + current prompt, 3 runs, on the same 150 (~$0.14). It separates the model effect from the prompt effect and gives a validated fallback. If (c) passes and the new prompt (b) does not beat it on gates 1-3, ship Haiku with the current prompt.
   - extra gate 4 item: the task suffix appears byte-exact in 100% of parsed haiku-run tasks. If not, see item 5 (code-side suffix).
   - runner drift: /tmp/router3t/run.py calls claude directly, not the chaude binary. It must load the prompt from the built code (e.g. a test helper that writes classifyPrompt to a file when an env flag is set) and check the sha256 from step b. Hand-copying the prompt into the runner is not allowed.

4. Rollback via CHAUDE_ROUTER_MODEL: confirmed as planned only. It does not exist yet.
   - fact: grep finds no CHAUDE_ROUTER_MODEL anywhere in internal/harness. The model is the const classifier.go:14 `conductorModel = "sonnet"`, used at :141. conductor_test.go:112 pins it to "sonnet". So today a rollback is a code revert. It becomes a config change only after change 1 ships.
   - decision: implement change 1 first, as its own step (default still sonnet, behavior unchanged), so the rollback path exists before the Haiku default goes live. Required details:
     a. the env value is trimmed and lowercased; allowed values are haiku|sonnet. An empty or invalid value -> routerModelDefault (not hard-coded "haiku" as the plan says), plus a one-time stderr warning. Otherwise a typo like "sonet" during a rollback would silently stay on haiku.
     b. couple prompt to model: keep the current prompt verbatim as classifyPromptSonnet and add classifyPromptHaiku. Select by the resolved model. Then CHAUDE_ROUTER_MODEL=sonnet restores exactly the validated pre-change behavior. The plan as written would run Sonnet with the untested Haiku prompt on rollback.
     c. read it in the chaude process (os.Getenv; cleanEnv only affects the child). Document that a running chaude must be restarted to pick it up.
     d. metrics stage=classify: add router_model and router_prompt (e.g. "haiku/v2", "sonnet/v1") so post-rollout cost and accuracy can be split.
     e. tests: replace conductor_test.go:112 with a table: unset -> default; "sonnet"/"SONNET " -> sonnet; "haiku" -> haiku; "opus"/"x" -> default; prompt selected matches model.
   - flipping the default to haiku after the gates pass is a one-line const change (routerModelDefault). Policy docs (CLAUDE.md:32, DECISIONS.md new line) change only after the pass, as the plan says.

5. 5-line output format: keep it now; decide later.
   - why: (a) changing model + prompt + format at once mixes up which change caused a result, and the gates could not attribute a failure; (b) a one-line format needs the parser (classifier.go:75-132) and worker/task handling rewritten, plus new parser tests, all outside a model-switch change; (c) the saving is small: the label prefixes are about 10 output tokens.
   - the real output cost is the long task suffix that the model retypes on every call, which is also a drift risk for Haiku. That is the next candidate and does not depend on the line format: the harness appends the suffix in code (parser adds it if it is missing), and the prompt asks only for the terse task. Do this as a follow-up only if the suffix gate in item 3 fails or the post-rollout metrics show output tokens dominating. Otherwise revisit the format after 1-2 weeks of router_model metrics.

## revised order
1. change 1 (env + two prompt constants + metrics fields + tests), default sonnet -> go test ./internal/harness.
2. tune the Haiku prompt on the dev set (30) -> freeze with sha256.
3. separate agent writes and freezes the 150-prompt test set (50/50/50, boundary <=10%) -> optional user label check (plan open q4) before any model call.
4. run: Sonnet+current x1, Haiku+new x3, Haiku+current x3, cap $3.
5. gates 1-4 (as revised) -> pass: routerModelDefault="haiku" (+ prompt choice per item 3) + docs; fail: stay on sonnet, record in LESSONS.md.

## [haiku] steps
- haiku-coder: classifier.go + conductor_test.go change 1 per item 4 a-e (one instance).
- haiku-drafter (fresh, no prompt text in brief): the 150-prompt test set per items 2-3.
- haiku-runner: the run in step 4, using the sha256-checked prompt dump.

## 변경 2: Haiku용 프롬프트 [결정 3]
순서: (a) 개발셋=기존 30프롬프트(notes/runs/261029-haiku-router-30-samples-list.md)로만 튜닝, 초안마다 Haiku 3회 -> (b) 동결, sha256을 평가셋 파일 머리말에 기록, 이후 수정 금지 -> (c) 별도 에이전트가 평가셋 작성(변경 3 검증 참조).
유지 조건:
- 출력: 정확히 5줄 topic/tier/kind/worker/task, 고정 어휘, "nothing else". "Always output topic, tier, kind and worker." 유지. [결정 5: 형식 유지]
- 현행 티어 규칙을 하나도 빼지 않는다. 초안에서 빠졌던 것 복원: "version bump with exact text"(haiku), "one-step edit of one file with a clear scope"(haiku), "clear multi-step task"/"comparison summary"(sonnet), "new feature or refactor with a given scope"->sonnet vs "design is open"->opus, "repeated failure", "'opus로'". 옛 문구 -> 새 문구 대응표를 평가셋 파일에 첨부.
- 어떤 규칙에도 안 맞으면 sonnet(절대 haiku 아님). haiku는 명시적 haiku 규칙 일치일 때만. 초안의 "first match opus->sonnet->haiku"는 무일치가 정의되지 않으므로 폐기.
- 동률 규칙은 현행 의미 그대로: "unsure haiku/sonnet -> sonnet; unsure sonnet/opus -> sonnet". 초안의 "항상 상위"는 채택하지 않음(opus 과분류 증가, 변수 혼입).
- topic: "When unsure, same." + 기존 new/same 정의. kind/worker: "A lookup or edit that is tier haiku is sent straight to a Haiku session", "worker only for kind edit, else new" 유지, "session.worker:" 빠진 공백만 수정.
- task 접미 'reply: Korean 존댓말, ... before replying' 은 바이트 단위 보존.
- 예시: 티어당 1개, 한국어, 전형적 사례, 개발셋/평가셋에 없는 새 문장. (초안의 예시 3개는 30샘플셋 출처라 사용 금지)
- 규칙은 영문, 한국어 트리거 단어는 괄호로 포함(설계, 트레이드오프, 추천, 전략, 원인, 계획, 'opus로').
- 길이 -30% 는 참고 지표(게이트 아님). 길이 때문에 규칙을 자르지 않는다.
- 구현 단위: `classifyPromptHaiku` 상수 작성 1건(haiku-coder, 문안은 튜닝 후 확정).

실행 3개 팔, 운영 인자 그대로, cwd 임시 디렉터리, env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, 누적 비용 $3 초과 시 중단:
- (a) Sonnet + 현행 프롬프트 x1 (기준선)
- (b) Haiku + 새 프롬프트 x3
- (c) Haiku + 현행 프롬프트 x3 (모델 효과와 프롬프트 효과 분리, 검증된 대체안)
- 총 150 + 450 + 450 = 1,050콜, 비용 약 $1.0 (Sonnet $0.68 + Haiku $0.14 x 2).
- 러너 드리프트 방지: /tmp/router3t/run.py 는 claude 직접 호출이므로, 빌드된 코드의 프롬프트를 덤프하는 테스트 헬퍼(env 플래그)로 파일에 쓰고 동결 sha256과 대조. 프롬프트 수동 복사 금지.
통과 기준 (b 기준, 전부 충족):
1. 누수: 비-haiku 기대인데 haiku로 보낸 서로 다른 프롬프트 수 = 0. 3회 중 한 번이라도 새면 그 프롬프트는 누수 1건. 하드 게이트. 참고: Sonnet 기준선 누수도 보고(Sonnet도 새면 라벨/규칙 문제).
2. 정확도(같은 프롬프트 쌍 비교, 3회 평균 오류 수):
   a. 전체: Haiku 오류 <= Sonnet 오류 + 3건(150의 2%p).
   b. 티어별: Haiku 오류 <= Sonnet 해당 티어 오류 + 2건.
   c. opus->sonnet 과소분류 <= Sonnet 기준선 + 2건.
3. 일관성: 150프롬프트 중 3회 모두 같은 티어 >= 90%.
4. 총 비용 <= $3; 파싱 실패 0건(재시도 후); tier 누락 0건; 파싱된 haiku 실행 task의 접미가 바이트 단위 100% 일치(실패 시 열린 질문 3의 코드측 접미).
참고 지표: 과대 분류 비율, 프롬프트 길이, 콜당 비용, Sonnet 기준선 변동.
(b)가 1-3에서 (c)보다 낫지 않고 (c)가 통과하면 Haiku + 현행 프롬프트로 출시.
재튜닝 금지: 실패 시 롤백. 이후 재튜닝은 새 평가셋(최소 실패 티어 50개 교체) 필요.

## 롤백
- 트리거: 기준 1-4 중 하나라도 실패.
- 조치: 기본값 sonnet 유지, 문서 미반영, 실패는 LESSONS.md 기록. 도입 후 롤백은 `CHAUDE_ROUTER_MODEL=sonnet`(설정만, 현행 프롬프트 복원, chaude 재시작).
- 운영 감시: router_model/router_prompt 메트릭으로 비용·정확도 분리. 정정/재요청 비율 지표는 미확인.

## 가정 (검증 방법)
1. 새 프롬프트에서도 누수 0 -> 기준 1 (30샘플 0/90은 구 프롬프트 기준).
2. 프롬프트 토큰 감소 -> usage input_tokens 측정(추정치 미측정).
3. 15배 비용 차이 유지 -> 러너 total_cost_usd 합.
4. `claude -p --model haiku` 운영 환경 동작 -> 3-tier 테스트 90/90로 확인, 재확인.
5. 파서 불변 -> 파서 단위 테스트 + 파싱 실패 0건.
6. 라벨이 사용자 의도와 일치 -> 경계 사례 사전 표시, 사용자 확인 요청.

## 순서 (단위)
1. 변경 1 구현(env + 프롬프트 상수 2개 + 메트릭 + 테스트, 기본 sonnet) -> go test ./internal/harness.
2. 개발셋 30개로 Haiku 프롬프트 튜닝 -> 동결(sha256).
3. 별도 에이전트가 150프롬프트 평가셋 작성·동결(50/50/50, 경계 <=10%) -> 선택적 사용자 라벨 확인.
4. 실행: (a) Sonnet+현행 x1, (b) Haiku+새 x3, (c) Haiku+현행 x3, 상한 $3.
5. 기준 1-4 판정 -> 통과: routerModelDefault="haiku"(+ 프롬프트 선택) + 변경 3 문서(사용자 승인 발언 확보 후); 실패: sonnet 유지, LESSONS.md.
위임: 1,2 haiku-coder; 3 haiku-drafter(새 인스턴스, 프롬프트 문안 비공개); 4 haiku-runner.

## 열린 질문
1. CLAUDE.md:32 의 `[routing: large ...]` 표현 정리는 별도 작업으로 둘지.
2. 평가셋 라벨을 사용자가 사전 확인할지(호출 전).
3. 후속 후보(지금 안 함): task 끝 문구('reply: Korean 존댓말...')를 코드가 붙이고 프롬프트는 간결한 task만 요청. 기준 4의 접미 검사 실패 또는 도입 후 출력 토큰이 지배적일 때, 5줄 형식 재검토는 1-2주 router_model 메트릭 이후.
4. DECISIONS.md 새 줄에 넣을 사용자 승인 발언 원문(미확보, 메인이 제공).

## 반영 기록
- 결정 1: 누수 0건을 하드 게이트로 유지, 서로 다른 프롬프트 기준 집계, 비-haiku 100개 이상, 경계 라벨 sonnet(10% 이하), Sonnet 누수는 참고 지표. 반영 위치: 검증.
- 결정 2: 평가셋 150(50/50/50, 티어당 최소 30), 전체 +3건 / 티어별 +2건 / opus->sonnet +2건 한도, 비용 약 $1.0으로 갱신, 50+50 구분 폐기. 반영 위치: 검증.
- 결정 3: 30샘플 개발셋 튜닝 -> 동결 -> 별도 에이전트 평가셋, 현행 규칙 전부 유지, 무일치=sonnet, 동률은 현행 의미(초안의 "항상 상위" 폐기), (c) Haiku+현행 팔 추가, 러너 sha256 대조. 반영 위치: 변경 2, 검증, 순서.
- 결정 4: CHAUDE_ROUTER_MODEL 먼저 구현(기본값·경고·프롬프트 상수 2개·메트릭 필드·테스트), 롤백은 설정만. 반영 위치: 변경 1, 롤백, 순서.
- 결정 5: 5줄 형식 유지, task 끝 문구 코드측 부착은 후속 후보. 반영 위치: 변경 2, 열린 질문 3.
- 기타: 길이 -30% 목표는 게이트에서 참고 지표로 강등(리뷰 3). 이전 열린 질문 1(한 줄+태그)은 결정 5로 닫음.

# review: 261029-plan-router-replace.md
verdict: 구조는 타당하나 게이트 정의가 haiku-policy 계획과 어긋나고 선행 구현 단계가 빠져 있어 수정 필요.
evidence: replace plan, haiku-policy plan (rev2) 직접 대조. DECISIONS.md는 grep(router/gate/rollback)만 확인했고 [conductor] 32행의 sonnet classifier 문구는 grep에 안 잡혀 미확인(정책 계획의 인용을 따름).

1. (S0 신설, S1 대체) CHAUDE_ROUTER_MODEL 구현 단계를 S2 앞에 넣는다. 이유: policy 계획은 이 env가 코드에 없다고 확인함(현재 롤백=코드 되돌리기). replace S1은 "처리 코드"를 조사한다고 적어 이미 있는 것처럼 읽히고, S6 "환경변수만으로 롤백"과 S4 (a)(c) 팔(현행 프롬프트)이 성립하려면 `routerModel()`, `classifyPromptSonnet`/`classifyPromptHaiku` 상수 2개, 메트릭 router_model/router_prompt, 테스트(conductor_test.go:112 교체)가 먼저 필요함. 기본값은 sonnet 유지.
2. (S5) 게이트를 policy와 같은 정의로 고친다. 현재 불일치:
   - "티어별 오류 각 2건 이하"는 절대값, policy는 "Sonnet 해당 티어 오류 + 2건". 절대값이면 Sonnet 자체가 3건 틀릴 때 무의미하게 실패.
   - "opus->sonnet 2건 이하"도 policy는 "Sonnet 기준선 + 2건".
   - "정확도 2%p 이내"와 "총 오류 +3건"은 150개에서 같은 조건이라 중복. 하나로 합친다(+3건).
   - 오류 집계 단위(3회 평균 vs 최악)를 명시: policy는 3회 평균 오류 수, 누수만 "한 번이라도 새면 1건".
3. (S5) 일관성 단위를 명시한다: "150프롬프트 중 3회 모두 같은 티어인 비율 >= 90%". 현재는 "3회 일관성 90%"만 있어 호출 단위(450콜)로도 읽힘.
4. (S5) 빠진 policy 게이트 추가: tier 누락 0건, 파싱 실패 0건(재시도 후), 파싱된 haiku 실행 task 접미('reply: Korean 존댓말...')가 바이트 단위 100% 일치. Sonnet 기준선 누수도 참고 보고(Sonnet도 새면 라벨/규칙 문제로 판정 보류).
5. (S4) 팔 (c)의 반복 횟수를 policy와 맞춘다. replace는 (b)만 3회, (c)는 x1로 읽힘. policy는 (c) x3(비교 가능성: 일관성/누수 비교는 같은 반복수여야 함). 콜 수 1,050.
6. (S4/S5) 팔 3개의 충분성: 모델 효과와 프롬프트 효과를 분리하는 데 충분하다. 단 판정 규칙이 빠져 있음 -> "(b)가 1-3에서 (c)보다 낫지 않고 (c)가 통과하면 Haiku+현행 프롬프트로 출시"(policy)를 추가하고, 그 경우 S6 전환 대상이 (b)가 아니라 (c)임을 적는다. 추가 팔(Sonnet+새 프롬프트)은 불필요(비용만 증가).
7. (S4) 비용 점검. 추정 $1.0(Sonnet 150콜 x $0.0045 = $0.68, Haiku 900콜 x $0.0003 = $0.27, 합 약 $0.95~1.0)은 $3 상한 안이고 여유 약 3배. 보완: (i) S2 튜닝 비용(30개 x 3회 x 초안 횟수)이 상한에 포함되는지 정하고 별도 집계, (ii) 실행 순서를 (a) -> (b) -> (c)로 고정하고 팔 단위로 누적 비용 기록, (iii) 상한 도달 시 중단하면 게이트 판정이 불가하므로 "중단=실패(sonnet 유지)"로 명시, (iv) 비용은 러너 total_cost_usd 합산으로 측정(콜당 15배 가정 재확인). 비용 게이트는 구독 인증이라 실제 청구가 아닌 보고 단가임을 한 줄 주석.
8. (S2~S3 순서) 동결 -> 평가셋 순서는 맞음. 추가 조건: 동결 sha256을 평가셋 머리말에 기록, 라벨은 어떤 모델 호출 전에 저장하고 이후 변경 금지, 작성 에이전트는 프롬프트 문안을 보지 않고 티어 정의만 보게 함, 경계 사례 라벨 sonnet + 사전 표시 + 세트의 10% 이하, 예시는 개발셋/평가셋에 없는 문장. replace S3엔 이들이 없다.
9. (S2) 러너 드리프트 방지: 러너(/tmp/router3t/run.py)에 프롬프트를 수동 복사하지 말고, 빌드된 코드의 프롬프트를 덤프하는 테스트 헬퍼로 파일에 쓰고 동결 해시와 대조한다. (a)(c)의 현행 프롬프트도 같은 방식으로 해시 기록.
10. (S2) 개발셋 과적합 방지: 알려진 오류 P2/L3/P8을 "우선 확인"하는 것은 좋지만, 해당 샘플에 맞춘 예시/키워드를 프롬프트에 넣지 않는다(예시 티어당 1개, 개발셋 문장 금지). 튜닝 횟수 상한(예: 초안 5회)과 "게이트 실패 시 재튜닝 금지, 재튜닝은 새 평가셋 필요" 규칙을 S5/S6에 추가.
11. (S7 vs S6 롤백 충돌 점검) deprecated 표기 자체는 롤백과 충돌하지 않으나 조건이 필요: `classifyPromptSonnet` 문안을 현행 바이트 그대로 유지(해시 테스트), 표기는 주석/문서 문자열만, 모델 허용값 sonnet 삭제 금지. 위험: 기본값 전환 후 오타/무효 env는 기본값(haiku)로 돌아가므로 롤백 중 오타가 조용히 haiku로 남음 -> policy처럼 stderr 경고 1회를 S0에 포함. S7은 S6 이후이고 S6의 롤백 검증 이후에 하도록 순서 고정.
12. (S8) 누락된 인수 검사 추가:
   - env 테스트: unset -> 기본값; "sonnet"/"SONNET " -> sonnet; "haiku" -> haiku; "opus"/"x" -> 기본값+경고.
   - 롤백 검증: 기본값을 haiku로 바꾼 뒤 `CHAUDE_ROUTER_MODEL=sonnet`에서 선택된 프롬프트 해시 == 변경 전 sonnet 프롬프트 해시, `--model sonnet`.
   - 파서 단위 테스트 통과(파서 불변 가정), 메트릭 stage=classify에 router_model/router_prompt 기록 확인.
   - 판정 결과 표(게이트별 수치, 통과/실패)를 notes/runs/에 저장, 실패 시 LESSONS.md 기록.
   - `go build/vet/test` 외에 CHAUDE_LIVE 미설정 시 라이브 테스트가 스킵되는지 확인.
13. (제약/S6) 정책 문서 미수정 제약과 S6 기본값 전환의 충돌 가능성: DECISIONS.md의 [conductor] 줄(policy 계획 기준 32행)이 sonnet classifier를 명시하므로, 문서 승인 없이 기본값을 바꾸면 코드와 결정 기록이 어긋남. 최소한 S6을 "승인 발언 확보 후"로 묶거나, 게이트 통과 후 전환 보류 + 승인 요청으로 처리. 현재 replace는 "승인 문구 없음"을 알면서 S6은 자동 전환으로 적혀 있음.
14. (실행 담당) S1은 haiku-scout 적절. S2는 "sonnet-analyst 설계 + haiku-coder 반영"이 불필요하게 두 단계 -> 프롬프트 튜닝은 haiku-coder 1개 인스턴스가 policy대로 수행, 판정(S5)만 sonnet-analyst. S3는 haiku-drafter 새 인스턴스(policy와 일치)로 명시.
15. (열린 질문) 두 번째 질문(약 $1 vs $3)은 위 7로 해결 가능하니 질문에서 빼고 계획에 수치 근거로 넣는다.

## 확정 필요 (사용자)
- S6 기본값 전환 및 CLAUDE.md:32 / DECISIONS.md 새 줄에 대한 승인 발언(원문). 없으면 게이트 통과해도 기본값은 sonnet 유지로 둘지.
- 프롬프트 변경 허용 범위: 의미 유지한 표현 변경까지만 vs 순서/예시 재구성 허용.
- 평가셋 라벨을 호출 전에 사용자가 확인할지(경계 사례 포함).
- 비용 $3 상한에 튜닝 비용을 포함할지.

# 계획 rev2: 라우터 교체 (Sonnet -> Haiku, Sonnet 라우터 deprecated)

요청 원문: "결과 다듬기, 라우터 교체, haiku 최적화 진행, sonnet 라우터는 deprecated 처리."
기반: 261029-plan-router-haiku-policy.md, 리뷰 반영본(261029-plan-router-replace-review.md 15항 중 채택분)
개발셋 30개: 261029-haiku-router-30-samples-list.md (라벨은 /tmp/router3t/run.py EXPECTED, 호출 전 확정)

## 제약
- 커밋/릴리스 없음. API 키 없음(cleanEnv, 구독 인증; 비용은 보고 단가이지 청구액 아님).
- CLAUDE.md, notes/DECISIONS.md 수정 금지(승인 없음). 수정안은 결과 노트에만 기재.
- 기본 라우터 모델은 사용자 승인 전까지 sonnet 유지. 게이트 통과해도 S6 전환은 하지 않고 "승인 대기"로 보고 (리뷰 13).
- 라이브 총비용(튜닝 포함) $3 상한. 도달 = 실패(sonnet 유지). 튜닝/평가 비용 별도 집계.

## 단계
- S0 (구현 잔여; 대부분 기존 코드에 있음): routerModel()/classifyPromptSonnet/Haiku/routerPrompt 존재 확인. 추가: 메트릭 router_prompt, Sonnet 프롬프트 sha256 고정 테스트, 프롬프트 덤프 테스트 헬퍼(CHAUDE_DUMP_PROMPTS=dir일 때만), env 테스트("SONNET " 포함). 기본값 sonnet 유지.
- S1 현황 조사: 위 코드로 확인 완료. 수정 대상: classifier.go 주석(S7), repl.go:60 주석. 비대상: CLAUDE.md, DECISIONS.md.
- S2 Haiku 프롬프트 튜닝: 개발셋 30개만. 기존 규칙 의미 유지(표현 변경과 "어느 규칙에도 안 맞으면 sonnet" 추가까지). 초안 최대 5회, 개발셋 문장/키워드를 예시로 넣지 않음(티어당 예시 1개 이하). 프롬프트는 덤프 파일에서 러너가 읽음(수동 복사 금지). 동결 sha256 기록. 현행 프롬프트 해시도 기록.
- S3 평가셋 150개: 동결 후 새 haiku-batch-worker 인스턴스가 티어 정의만 보고 작성(프롬프트 문안 비공개). 티어당 50개, 비-haiku 100개, 개발셋과 겹침 0(정규화 완전일치 검사), 경계 사례는 sonnet 라벨+표시+10% 이하, 머리말에 동결 sha256, 라벨은 호출 전 고정.
- S4 라이브(순서 고정 a->b->c, 팔 단위 누적비용 기록, 러너 total_cost_usd 합산): (a) Sonnet+현행 x1, (b) Haiku+새 x3, (c) Haiku+현행 x3. 150프롬프트, 총 1,050콜 예상 약 $1.0 (Sonnet $0.0045/콜, Haiku $0.0003/콜 실측 기반).
- S5 게이트 판정(오류 = 3회 평균, 누수는 한 번이라도 새면 1건):
  - 누수(비-haiku 프롬프트 -> haiku) 0, 고유 프롬프트 기준, 비-haiku 표본 >= 100. Sonnet 기준선 누수도 보고.
  - 총 오류 <= Sonnet + 3건
  - 티어별 오류 <= Sonnet 해당 티어 + 2건
  - opus->sonnet <= Sonnet 기준선 + 2건
  - 일관성: 150프롬프트 중 3회 모두 같은 티어 >= 90%
  - tier 누락 0, 파싱 실패 0(재시도 후)
  - haiku 실행 task 접미('reply: Korean 존댓말...') 바이트 일치 100%
  - 비용 <= $3
  - 판정 규칙: (b)가 (c)보다 낫지 않고 (c)가 통과하면 (c)(현행 프롬프트)로 전환 대상 변경.
  - 게이트 실패 시 재튜닝 금지(재튜닝은 새 평가셋 필요).
- S6 기본값 전환: 수행하지 않음(승인 대기). 통과 시 필요한 변경과 롤백 검증 계획만 기록.
- S7 deprecated 표기: classifyPromptSonnet 바이트 유지(해시 테스트), 주석/문서 문자열만, 허용값 sonnet 유지. repl.go:60 주석을 실제 동작에 맞게 정정. 기본값이 sonnet이므로 "default to be replaced after approval"로 표기.
- S8 검증: go build/vet/test, CHAUDE_LIVE 미설정 시 라이브 스킵, 판정표를 notes/runs/에 저장, sonnet-reviewer로 최종 diff 검토.

## 담당
S0/S7: haiku-coder. S2: 설계는 본 에이전트, 프롬프트 반영은 haiku-coder. S3: haiku-batch-worker(독립). S4/S8: haiku-runner. S5: 본 에이전트. 완료 전 sonnet-reviewer.

## 열린 질문(사용자)
- S6 전환과 CLAUDE.md:32 / DECISIONS.md 수정 승인 문구.
- 평가셋 경계 사례 라벨을 호출 전 사용자가 확인할지.

=== notes/runs/261029-plan-routing-review.md (mtime 2026-10-29) ===
# chaude 라우팅 구조 검토 (읽기 전용, 코드 수정 없음)

## Q1. "Haiku가 분류·처리하고, 어려울 때만 Opus/Sonnet 호출" 구조가 맞는가
결론: 처리 구조는 맞지만 분류는 Haiku가 아니라 Sonnet이 합니다. 문서와 구현이 일부 어긋납니다.

근거(사실)
- 분류기는 매 프롬프트마다 별도 `claude -p --model sonnet` 일회성 호출입니다 (internal/harness/classifier.go:14 conductorModel="sonnet", :109-:115 classify). 도구 없음, 세션 없음, cwd=tmpdir (classifier.go:115-117).
- 분류 결과는 topic/size/kind/worker/task 5줄 태그뿐입니다 (classifier.go:14-15). 답변은 생성하지 않습니다.
- 메인 세션은 Haiku 고정입니다. pickModel은 cur가 ""/haiku면 항상 haiku를 반환하고 (classifier.go:38-41), pickTarget도 kind와 무관하게 Haiku입니다 (classifier.go:49-51). 강제 --model sonnet|opus만 유지됩니다.
- size=large면 planHint가 붙습니다 (classifier.go:92-95 (분기 :94)). Haiku가 계획 작성 -> opus-architect/sonnet-analyst가 개선안만 작성 -> Haiku가 병합·실행, Opus/Sonnet은 실행하지 않습니다 (classifier.go:31-34). 즉 "Haiku가 어렵다고 판단해서 호출"이 아니라 "Sonnet 분류기가 large로 태깅 -> 힌트 -> Haiku가 호출"입니다.
- 문서도 같은 내용입니다: CLAUDE.md:31 (Haiku-fixed main, classifier always Sonnet and only tags size), DECISIONS.md:32 (Sonnet 일회성 분류기), :38 (pickModel/pickTarget이 haiku 반환, planHint).

문서 vs 구현 차이
- CLAUDE.md:2 헤더와 :9의 "Opus main" 라우팅 문단은 강제 Opus main일 때만 적용되는 구 규칙입니다 (CLAUDE.md:31 마지막 문장이 명시). 읽는 사람이 혼동하기 쉽습니다.
- DECISIONS.md:30-33은 "Sonnet이 답/위임 대상을 정한다 (target=haiku|sonnet|opus)"는 이전 설계를 기록하고, :38이 이를 덮어씁니다. 현재 구현에서 분류기의 model 출력은 사실상 무의미(항상 haiku)합니다. 의견: 분류기 프롬프트의 kind/worker 중 worker만 의미가 남아 프롬프트가 필요 이상으로 깁니다.
- 분류 단계가 Sonnet이라 "Haiku가 판단"이라는 직관과 다릅니다. 매 프롬프트 Sonnet 비용이 별도 발생합니다 (metrics stage=classify, DECISIONS.md:32).
- 어려움 판단의 주체: 구현상 Sonnet 분류기 1회. Haiku는 힌트가 있을 때만 호출 순서를 따릅니다. Haiku 자체가 난이도를 재판단해 에스컬레이션하는 코드는 확인하지 못했습니다 (확인 범위: classifier.go 전체, CLAUDE.md, DECISIONS.md grep).

## Q2. Opus/Sonnet을 서브에이전트가 아닌 메인 세션으로 돌리는 편이 토큰 효율적인가
결론(의견, 정량 측정 없음): 이 프로젝트의 기본 사용 패턴에서는 서브에이전트가 유리하고, 같은 파일·같은 작업줄기를 여러 턴 이어갈 때만 메인 세션이 유리합니다.

비용 구조(일반 원리, 이 저장소 수치로 검증하지 않음)
- 서브에이전트: 호출당 새 컨텍스트. 비용 = 브리프 + 에이전트 자체 탐색/도구 출력 + 결과 요약. 메인 히스토리를 다시 읽지 않습니다. 단점: 호출마다 시스템 프롬프트·CLAUDE.md를 새로 읽고(캐시 쓰기), 같은 파일을 반복 호출 시 재탐색합니다.
- 메인 세션: 전체 히스토리를 매 턴 다시 읽습니다. 캐시가 살아 있으면 읽기 단가(싸다)지만 컨텍스트가 커질수록 턴당 비용이 선형 증가하고, TTL이 지나면 전체가 쓰기 단가로 재청구됩니다. Opus/Sonnet 단가가 Haiku보다 높아 이 효과가 커집니다.

이 프로젝트 조건(사실)
- 이미 컨텍스트 증가를 제어하는 장치가 많습니다: 270k 이상 회전 (DECISIONS.md:16), 유휴 회전 (:19-:23), 자동 compact 150k (CLAUDE.md:26). 이는 메인 세션 컨텍스트 증가 비용이 실제 관심사임을 보여줍니다.
- 연구(scout/researcher)는 서브에이전트 유지로 결정됐고, 코드 수정·분석·집필·배치·runner는 "세션 워커" 후보로 비교 실험 중입니다 (DECISIONS.md:25, :27). 아직 측정 결과는 없습니다 (미검증).

각 방식이 이기는 조건 (의견)
- 서브에이전트 승: 일회성·독립 작업, 탐색/검색이 큰 출력(결과 요약만 필요), 병렬 작업, 메인이 Haiku라 히스토리가 싼 경우, 캐시 TTL이 자주 끊기는 간헐적 사용.
- 메인 Opus/Sonnet 승: 같은 파일·결정 맥락을 연속 5-10턴 이상 이어가는 설계/디버깅 대화, 브리프로 압축하기 어려운 맥락(미묘한 사용자 정정 이력), 캐시가 살아 있어 읽기 단가가 적용되는 연속 사용. 브리프가 히스토리만큼 길어지면 서브에이전트 이점이 사라집니다.
- 혼합 지점: Opus 메인에서 서브에이전트 호출 시 Opus가 히스토리 재독 + 서브에이전트 비용을 이중 부담 (CLAUDE.md:9 "Opus delegating to Opus saves nothing"이 같은 취지).

## 권고
현행 유지(Haiku 메인 + Sonnet 분류 + Opus/Sonnet 서브에이전트 설계 검토)를 기본으로, 연속 작업줄기에 한해 세션 워커를 DECISIONS.md:27 실험으로 측정한 뒤 결정합니다. 추가로 metrics의 classify 비용과 에이전트별 토큰을 근거로 삼으세요.
주요 위험: (1) 매 프롬프트 Sonnet 분류 오버헤드가 소규모 프롬프트에서 Haiku 처리비보다 클 수 있음, (2) Sonnet이 size를 잘못 태깅하면 Haiku가 어려운 작업을 직접 수행해 재작업 비용 발생, (3) 위 비용 비교는 측정치 없는 추정입니다.
미해결 질문: classify 호출의 평균 비용 대비 Haiku 처리비 비율 (notes/metrics/*.jsonl에서 stage=classify 집계 필요, 이번에 집계하지 않음).

No accessor on Repl/Session needed." Drop `progress()` accessor for main; delete the open item about Session.Events for main. S1 test TestSpecterProgressNoIO then only covers the subagent accessor (item 4).

2. [F] Agent summary in UI is the LAST plain-text line of the streamed log, not the first line; async agents may have none.

   - plan edit (c)/S4: either (A) put the "did:" content as the LAST line of the final message, or (B) add code: onNotification/onToolResult extract the result text and set Summary from its first line.    - fact: the Agent tool_result (foreground) / <task-notification> (async) body enters the main model context in full; the TUI first/last line is only a display. DECISIONS 36 already says main "posts" the summary -> main re-emits it as output tokens too (counted twice). [I] Haiku main rotates at 80k (DECISIONS 41), so per-agent overhead matters there most.
   - plan edit (c): "did:" must REPLACE the outcome field of the existing summary, not add a line. So the user's "specter on opus/sonnet" maps mostly to subagent rows (S3), which depend on the background fix. # Plan: haiku-specter (live progress reporter for the main session)
date: 2026-10-29
status: plan only, no code changed, no agent file created
basis:
- notes/runs/261029-analysis-progress-output.md (progress is feasible in memory: elapsed time, last tool use; subagent token progress not collected)
- notes/runs/261029-plan-local-commands.md (local command plan; its open decisions are numbered 1-9 in that file, the brief called them U1-U7)
- notes/runs/261029-diag-background-panel.md (background agents missing from panel; fix not applied)
- notes/DECISIONS.md lines 36, 38-41 (return-summary rule; Haiku main policy)
legend: [F] fact from notes/source | [I] inference | [U] user decision needed

## user design (quoted, Korean)
- haiku-specter = "메인 세션(opus/sonnet)에 붙어 메인의 중간 진행 상황을 사용자에게 보고하는 에이전트."
- "일반 haiku 에이전트는 각 작업을 끝낼 때마다 무엇을 했는지 추가로 보고."
- "명령 실행을 모델 없이 Go로 처리하는 것과 함께 반영."

## core decisions (proposed)
1. specter is NOT a model. It is an in-memory display in the harness (Go, TUI process). Zero model tokens per tick. [I] Reason: a Haiku agent per tick costs tokens and adds latency; the user asked for Go for command execution too. [U] D1 confirms.
2. Regular Haiku agents report "what they did" through the existing result path only (final message, first line shown in UI). No new file, no new channel. [F] DECISIONS 36 already sets the final-message rule.
3. Sequencing: background-panel fix first, then specter display. Local-command work is independent (0 tokens) and can run in parallel. [F] analysis recommends defer-then-do; [I] specter value for subagents depends on the fix.

## (a) what specter is, and what it must not do
Is:
- A status strip/row in the TUI that shows the main session's current activity: running state, elapsed time, last tool use (e.g. `● Read(path)`).
- Read-only view of harness memory.

Must not:
- Read files on behalf of main, or make main read files for progress. [F] Analysis: display reads happen in TUI memory, not model context.
- Add tokens to the main prompt or to any model call. [F] analysis: "do not feed progress to main model (would grow context)."
- Cost a model call per tick. Tick = 8 Hz spinner already calling running() [F tui.go:327, 372-378]; accessor must be lock + copy only.
- Write a status file or poll agents.json. [F] agents.json poll ~21 KB/read, changes only on state transitions; unsuitable.
- Call /usage or `claude -p` for progress. [F] unsuitable.

## (b) how it gets main-session progress
- Source: events the harness already receives from the claude child and renders (assistant text streaming, tool `● Name(arg)` lines). [F] DECISIONS [tui] line 12 (TUI shows these for main). [U] Whether the same event stream carries usable per-tool timing: unverified; Session.Events body not read (analysis open item).
- Store only in memory: `turnStartedAt` (time), `lastToolLine` (string, last tool use). Set on event receipt. No history kept beyond the last line.
- Accessor: `progress() (elapsed time.Duration, lastTool string, running bool)`. Must not copy the full log per tick (analysis: do NOT call snapshot() per tick, copies up to 400 lines).
- Render: one row/line near the status line; updated by existing spinner tick.
- Token progress for main: not in scope. Main token usage already appears per turn (usageLine). [F] DECISIONS [tui] status line shows ctx/threshold.
- Model choice (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku main): see D2.

## (c) what regular Haiku agents report after each task
- Existing path: the agent's final message is returned via the Agent tool result; the TUI shows its first line. [F] analysis line 8.
- Content rule (already in all 11 .claude/agents/*.md, DECISIONS 36): "Final message = only a brief result summary (a few lines, Korean 존댓말: outcome · changed paths · PASS/FAIL) ... full details go to `notes/runs/`, give only the path."
- Proposed addition for "무엇을 했는지": one extra line "did: <what was done, 1 line>" as the first line of the final message. [U] D5 confirms wording and whether it is required for haiku-* only.
- No new output file. Details stay in notes/runs/.
- Haiku agents are async by default now [F diag: Agent tool_use has no run_in_background], so the completion line only reaches the UI after the background-panel fix (see d).

## (d) relation to background-panel fix and local-command plan
Background panel (notes/runs/261029-diag-background-panel.md):
- [F] Background agents are marked Done at launch (drain.go:72-77), so they vanish from the panel. Specter's subagent rows depend on this fix.
- [F] Fix location: drain.go:62-63, :75; treat "Async agent launched" tool_result as background, do not mark Done.
- Order: fix -> commit -> specter subagent rows. [I]
- Main-session progress (b) does not depend on this fix.

Local-command plan (notes/runs/261029-plan-local-commands.md):
- [F] Local commands = 0 model tokens by design. Specter adds no tokens either, so both fit the "no model per tick" rule.
- Dependency: /rotate and /model <name> use a model handoff turn today (its decision 1-2). If specter reports rotation, it reports whatever the handoff does. No specter change needed for either choice.
- Dependency: /agents (its decision 6) would show the same tracker rows as specter. Choose one row source; do not build two. [I]
- Local plan's open decisions 1-9 are NOT answered here. [U] remain open there.
- Name conflict: the local plan notes no agent named haiku-specter exists; nearest is haiku-scout (model haiku, effort high). [F]

## (e) acceptance per step
S1 accessor (in-memory only)
- Test TestSpecterProgressNoIO: run a fake turn with events; assert no file created under state dir and no claude child spawned for the accessor.
- Test TestSpecterAccessorNoCopy: accessor does not call snapshot(); assert via benchmark or code grep that it touches only the last line.
S2 TUI row (main progress)
- Test TestSpecterRowRenders: with running turn and lastTool "● Read(x)", row contains elapsed and "Read(x)"; with idle turn row absent.
- Manual: capture in notes/runs/ with a live run (not yet done).
S3 subagent rows (after background fix)
- Test TestBackgroundAgentShownRunning: Agent tool_use without run_in_background + "Async agent launched" result -> running row present, not Done.
- Test: completion via <task-notification> marks Done.
S4 Haiku final line
- grep: each .claude/agents/haiku-*.md contains the return-summary line (DECISIONS 36) and, if D5 = yes, the "did:" line.
- Check: UI first line of a finished agent equals the "did:" line (test with fixture result).
S5 no-token guarantee (whole feature)
- Count model calls during a 60s idle + 60s running window with specter enabled: expected 0 extra calls. Measure with fake claude that logs argv; assert log has only the real turn's calls.

Each step: go test ./internal/harness/... passes; no new file under notes/ except notes/runs/ entries.

## (f) user decisions (separate list; none answered by this plan)
- D1. specter = Go in-memory display (recommended, 0 tokens) OR a Haiku agent that polls (costs tokens per tick; not recommended). [U]
- D2. Main models specter attaches to: brief says opus/sonnet, but DECISIONS 38-41 make Haiku the main default (Opus only for design; Haiku rotates at 80k). Confirm: all mains, or only Opus/Sonnet? [U]
- D3. Name: keep "haiku-specter" (only if it is a model-backed agent file), or use a non-agent name since D1 is Go-only? [U]
- D4. Progress content: elapsed + last tool line only (analysis recommendation), no token progress. Confirm. [U]
- D5. Haiku final line: add a "did: <1 line>" first line for haiku-* agents (brief asks "무엇을 했는지"), or keep the existing summary only? [U]
- D6. Order: background-panel fix first, then specter subagent rows (analysis recommendation)? Or specter first? [U]

Count of user decisions: 6 (D1-D6). Local-command decisions 1-9 are a separate list in its own file.

## open / uncertain
- Session.Events body not read; per-tool timing and whether main events carry usable usage: unverified.
- Background-panel diagnosis not runtime-verified (no live TUI run).
- "elapsed" is inference from started field (agentstore.go:28-43); main-turn start time source not verified.
- No file in repo changed by this plan.
